Subject: Changes to forecast categories + training invite (Commit / Best Case / Pipeline)

Hi team,

Quick note to share a small but important change to how we label and surface opportunities in our forecast exports. After the last ops review we found a handful of recurring misclassifications that are skewing weekly rollups — primarily between Commit and Best Case and some ambiguous Pipeline stage mappings.

What we are changing (summary):
- Commit: opportunities with signed commercial terms or an approved PO (finance/legal holds are acceptable if a PO is present). Commit must reflect predictable close in the current period.
- Best Case: higher-probability but not-confirmed deals (verbal acceptance, budget allocated, awaiting final PO).
- Pipeline: early-stage opportunities that require discovery, qualification, or budget approval.

Why it matters: correct labels improve our capacity planning and Dedicated capacity sizing. Small changes propagate to billing forecasts and quota attainment models.

What I need from this group:
1) Please review the attached mapping spreadsheet (forecast-category-mapping-v2.xlsx) and flag any rows where the stage in your territories doesn't match the proposed mapping by EOD Thursday (2027-06-24).
2) Join the hands-on dry run on Tue 2027-07-06 (30m) where we'll walk through HubSpot examples and run a commit-review lab. Calendar invite attached (dryrun-agenda-2027-07-06.ics).
3) For customer-facing teams: update the opportunity-level "Category" field to match definitions prior to the weekly commit review on 2027-07-08.

Attachments: forecast-category-mapping-v2.xlsx, commit-bestcase-guidelines-v1.3.pdf, dryrun-agenda-2027-07-06.ics

Thanks — keeping this lightweight but we need consistent application across regions.

—Olga

Thanks, Olga — appreciate the clear definitions. Two quick clarifying questions before I push changes to my book of business: 

1) How should we treat deals in "Legal review" where commercial terms are signed but legal is still negotiating minor SOW language? If a countersigned contract is not yet in hand but the customer has provided an approval email, do we mark as Commit or Best Case?

2) For opportunities where an internal vendor PO is issued but the customer billing is scheduled next quarter (vendor takes the payment now), should that be Commit for us?

Example context: I have an opportunity (Nimbus-2027-Q3) where the customer sent an "approval to proceed" email but legal flagged a line-item to clarify scope. I assume that sits in Best Case until countersignature, but want to confirm given the PO/approval nuance.

—Karthik

Karthik — good questions. Short answers and a couple of practical rules to keep things consistent: 

- Legal review with signed commercial terms: If a customer has provided a signed order form or a written PO/approval that commits budget, mark as Commit. If only the commercial terms were agreed verbally and we are waiting for countersignature, mark as Best Case.

- Vendor PO vs customer billing timing: Commit is about commercial intent and verifiability (signed PO / signed contract / approved purchase order). If the vendor PO is internal and doesn't equate to customer confirmation, treat carefully — default to Best Case unless you have a customer-sourced PO or a definitive billing authorization.

Practical stage mapping (suggested bullets to copy into CRM mapping):
- Legal: countersign pending — Best Case (unless signed PO attached)
- PO issued by customer (scanned / email) — Commit
- Verbal approval + budget allocated — Best Case
- Negotiation / scope clarification — Pipeline

Also, Karthik: please bring the Nimbus-2027-Q3 example to the dry run; we'll run a quick mock commit review. I've asked Monica to invite SDRs for one slot so we can cover qualification edge cases.

—Laura
